subject.name: Chemistry
subject.description: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry. Core students take Papers 1 and 3; Extended students take Papers 2 and 4. The practical papers (5 and 6) are not included. The questions are original practice questions written in the style of Cambridge papers, not reproduced past paper material.

topics.title: States of matter
topics.summary: Solids, liquids and gases, changes of state, diffusion.

topics.title: Atoms, elements and compounds
topics.summary: Atomic structure, isotopes, ions and ionic bonds, covalent bonds, giant structures, metallic bonding.

topics.title: Stoichiometry
topics.summary: Formulae, equations, relative masses and the mole.

topics.title: Chemical energetics
topics.summary: Exothermic and endothermic reactions, bond energies.

topics.title: Chemical reactions
topics.summary: Physical and chemical changes, rate of reaction, reversible reactions and equilibrium, redox.

topics.title: Acids, bases and salts
topics.summary: Properties of acids and bases, oxides, preparation of salts.

topics.title: The Periodic Table
topics.summary: Arrangement of elements, Group I, Group VII, transition elements, noble gases.

topics.title: Metals
topics.summary: Properties and uses, alloys, reactivity series, corrosion, extraction.

topics.title: Chemistry of the environment
topics.summary: Water, fertilisers, air quality and climate.

topics.title: Organic chemistry
topics.summary: Formulae and homologous series, alkanes, alkenes, alcohols, carboxylic acids, polymers.

topics.title: Experimental techniques and chemical analysis
topics.summary: Experimental design, titrations, chromatography, separation and purification, identification of ions and gases.

parts.prompt: Which change of state is a solid turning directly into a gas?
parts.examinerComment: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas, as with solid carbon dioxide.

parts.prompt: Which gas diffuses fastest at the same temperature?
parts.examinerComment: Gases with a lower relative molecular mass diffuse faster. Hydrogen has Mᵣ = 2.

parts.prompt: An atom has 11 protons and 12 neutrons. What is its nucleon number?
parts.examinerComment: Nucleon number = protons + neutrons.

parts.prompt: Which substance has a giant covalent structure?
parts.examinerComment: Sodium chloride is giant ionic; methane is simple molecular; copper is metallic.

parts.prompt: What is the relative formula mass of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃?
What volume does 0.50 mol of a gas occupy at room temperature and pressure?
parts.examinerComment: One mole of any gas occupies 24 dm³ at r.t.p.

parts.prompt: Molten lead(II) bromide is electrolysed. What forms at the cathode?
parts.examinerComment: Positive lead ions are attracted to the negative cathode and gain electrons.

parts.prompt: Concentrated aqueous sodium chloride is electrolysed. What forms at the anode?
parts.examinerComment: Hydrogen forms at the cathode. Sodium is never produced from aqueous solutions.

parts.prompt: What happens to the temperature of the surroundings during an exothermic reaction?
parts.examinerComment: Exothermic reactions transfer thermal energy to the surroundings.

parts.prompt: Which statement about bonds is correct?
parts.examinerComment: Energy is needed to break bonds; energy is released when bonds form.

parts.prompt: Why does increasing the temperature increase the rate of a reaction?

options.text: Particles have more kinetic energy, so there are more frequent successful collisions.
The concentration of the reactants increases.

markingPoints.text: C – Particles have more kinetic energy, so there are more frequent successful collisions.

parts.examinerComment: Answers should refer to more collisions per second with energy greater than the activation energy.

parts.prompt: What is oxidation in terms of electrons?
parts.examinerComment: Remember OIL RIG: oxidation is loss, reduction is gain.

parts.prompt: What is the pH of a neutral solution?
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Which salt is made when dilute sulfuric acid reacts with aqueous sodium hydroxide?
parts.examinerComment: Sulfuric acid forms sulfates; sulfides contain no oxygen.

parts.prompt: How does the reactivity of Group I metals change down the group?
parts.examinerComment: The outer electron is further from the nucleus and is lost more easily.

parts.prompt: Why are the noble gases unreactive?

options.text: They have a full outer shell of electrons.

markingPoints.text: B – They have a full outer shell of electrons.

parts.examinerComment: Noble gases are monatomic, so option D is wrong.

parts.prompt: Which metal is extracted from bauxite by electrolysis?
parts.examinerComment: Iron and zinc are extracted by reduction with carbon.

parts.prompt: What is needed for iron to rust?
parts.examinerComment: Experiments with drying agents and boiled water show both are needed.

parts.prompt: Which gas is the main cause of acid rain?
parts.examinerComment: Carbon dioxide contributes to climate change, not significantly to acid rain.

parts.prompt: Approximately what percentage of clean, dry air is nitrogen?
parts.examinerComment: Oxygen is about 21%.

parts.prompt: What is the general formula of the alkanes?
parts.examinerComment: CₙH₂ₙ is the general formula of the alkenes.

parts.prompt: Which observation shows that a hydrocarbon is an alkene?

options.text: It burns with a blue flame.

parts.examinerComment: Aqueous bromine changes from orange to colourless.

parts.prompt: Which method separates sand from water?
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: How is the Rf value in chromatography calculated?

options.text: distance moved by solvent ÷ distance moved by substance
distance moved by substance ÷ distance moved by solvent
distance moved by substance − distance moved by solvent
distance moved by substance × distance moved by solvent

markingPoints.text: B – distance moved by substance ÷ distance moved by solvent

parts.examinerComment: Rf values are always less than 1.

parts.prompt: Describe the arrangement and motion of the particles in a liquid.

markingPoints.text: close together, in an irregular (random) arrangement
particles move / slide past each other

parts.examinerComment: Some candidates described a gas. Liquid particles are still touching.

parts.prompt: An atom of chlorine is represented by ³⁷₁₇Cl. State the number of protons, neutrons and electrons in this atom.
parts.examinerComment: The neutron number is 37 − 17.

parts.prompt: Calculate the relative formula mass of ammonium sulfate, (NH₄)₂SO₄.
parts.examinerComment: Multiplying the whole NH₄ group by 2 was essential.

parts.prompt: State what is meant by electrolysis.

markingPoints.text: when molten or in aqueous solution, by the passage of an electric current

parts.examinerComment: Answers must state that the compound is broken down.

parts.prompt: The temperature of a reaction mixture rises from 21 °C to 34 °C. State the temperature change and whether the reaction is exothermic or endothermic.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Marble chips react with dilute hydrochloric acid. State two ways to increase the rate of this reaction.

markingPoints.text: increase the concentration of the acid

parts.examinerComment: 'Add more acid' is not the same as increasing its concentration.

parts.prompt: Name the gas produced when zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid, and give a test for it.

markingPoints.text: a lighted splint gives a squeaky pop

parts.examinerComment: A glowing splint is the test for oxygen.

parts.prompt: Name the two products formed when potassium reacts with water.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Explain why alloys are often used instead of pure metals.

markingPoints.text: different-sized atoms disrupt the layers so they cannot slide easily

parts.examinerComment: The best answers explained the structure as well as stating the property.

parts.prompt: Describe a chemical test for water.

markingPoints.text: turns from white to blue (or cobalt(II) chloride from blue to pink)

parts.examinerComment: Both the reagent and the colour change are needed.

parts.prompt: Name the functional group present in ethanol.
parts.examinerComment: 'Hydroxide' is incorrect: that is an ion.

parts.prompt: In a chromatography experiment, a spot moves 3.0 cm and the solvent front moves 7.5 cm. Calculate the Rf value.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

questions.stem: A solid is heated steadily. Fig. 1 shows how its temperature changes.

figures.alt: Heating curve: temperature rises from 20 °C to 80 °C in 4 minutes, stays at 80 °C until 9 minutes, then rises to 130 °C at 14 minutes.
figures.caption: Fig. 1

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use Fig. 1 to find the melting point of the substance, in °C.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why the temperature stays constant between 4 and 9 minutes.

markingPoints.text: energy is used to overcome the forces between particles instead of raising the temperature

parts.examinerComment: Many said 'no energy is being supplied', but heating continues throughout.

questions.stem: Marble chips react with dilute hydrochloric acid. Fig. 2 shows the volume of carbon dioxide collected.

figures.alt: Graph of volume of gas against time: the volume rises steeply at first, then levels off at 60 cm³ after about 60 s.
figures.caption: Fig. 2

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use Fig. 2 to find the total volume of gas produced, in cm³.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use Fig. 2 to find the volume of gas collected after 20 s, in cm³.
parts.examinerComment: Read carefully from the curve.

questions.stem: Fig. 3 shows the chromatogram of two dyes, A and B, and a mixture, X.

figures.alt: Chromatogram: the solvent front is 8.0 cm above the baseline. Dye A gives one spot at 2.0 cm, dye B one spot at 6.0 cm, and mixture X two spots at 2.0 cm and 6.0 cm.
figures.caption: Fig. 3

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Which dyes does mixture X contain? Explain your answer.

markingPoints.text: its spots are at the same heights as the spots of A and B

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the Rf value of dye A.
parts.examinerComment: Measure from the baseline, not the bottom of the paper.

parts.prompt: Ammonia and hydrogen chloride gases are released at opposite ends of a long tube. A white ring of ammonium chloride forms nearer the hydrogen chloride end. Explain why.

markingPoints.text: ammonia has a lower Mᵣ (17) than hydrogen chloride (36.5)
so ammonia travels further before the gases meet

parts.examinerComment: Candidates should compare relative molecular masses using numbers.

parts.prompt: Explain why sodium chloride has a high melting point.

markingPoints.text: strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions
a lot of energy is needed to overcome these forces

parts.examinerComment: References to 'strong bonds' without saying what type did not earn full credit.

parts.prompt: Calcium carbonate decomposes on heating: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. Calculate the mass of calcium oxide formed from 25 g of calcium carbonate, in g.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Write the ionic half-equation for the reaction at the cathode when copper is deposited from aqueous copper(II) sulfate.

markingPoints.text: Cu²⁺ and e⁻ on the left, Cu on the right

parts.examinerComment: Electrons must be gained at the cathode.

parts.prompt: Use the bond energies to calculate the energy change for H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl, in kJ/mol. Bond energies: H–H 436, Cl–Cl 242, H–Cl 431 kJ/mol.
parts.examinerComment: The negative sign shows the reaction is exothermic and is required.

parts.prompt: In the Haber process, N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ and the forward reaction is exothermic. State and explain the effect on the yield of ammonia of increasing the pressure.

markingPoints.text: the position of equilibrium shifts to the right
because there are fewer moles of gas on the right (2 compared with 4)

parts.examinerComment: Answers should refer to the number of moles of gas on each side.

parts.prompt: 25.0 cm³ of aqueous sodium hydroxide is neutralised by 20.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid. Calculate the concentration of the sodium hydroxide, in mol/dm³.
parts.examinerComment: Converting cm³ to dm³ was the most common source of error.

parts.prompt: Chlorine is bubbled into aqueous potassium bromide. Explain what happens and write the ionic equation.

markingPoints.text: chlorine is more reactive than bromine, so it displaces it

parts.examinerComment: Potassium ions are spectator ions and are left out of the ionic equation.

parts.prompt: Write the balanced equation for the reduction of iron(III) oxide by carbon monoxide in the blast furnace.

markingPoints.text: correct formulae: Fe₂O₃, CO, Fe, CO₂

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Explain how a catalytic converter reduces air pollution from car engines.

markingPoints.text: carbon monoxide is converted to carbon dioxide
oxides of nitrogen are converted to nitrogen

parts.examinerComment: Both pollutants and their products were needed for full marks.

parts.prompt: Ethanoic acid reacts with ethanol to form an ester. Name the ester and state the conditions needed.

markingPoints.text: concentrated sulfuric acid as a catalyst, with heating

parts.examinerComment: 'Ethanoyl ethanol' and 'ethyl ethanol' were common incorrect names.

parts.prompt: Describe a test for ammonium ions in a solution.

markingPoints.text: add aqueous sodium hydroxide and warm
which turns damp red litmus paper blue

parts.examinerComment: The litmus paper must be damp.

questions.stem: Marble chips react with dilute hydrochloric acid. Fig. 2 shows the volume of carbon dioxide collected.

figures.alt: Graph of volume of gas against time: the volume rises steeply at first, then levels off at 60 cm³ after about 60 s.
figures.caption: Fig. 2

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain, in terms of particles, why the rate of reaction decreases as the reaction proceeds.

markingPoints.text: the concentration of acid decreases / fewer acid particles
so there are fewer collisions per second

parts.examinerComment: Answers should refer to the frequency of collisions.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: On the same axes, a student repeats the experiment with powdered marble of the same mass. Describe how the new curve would differ.

markingPoints.text: levels off at the same final volume, 60 cm³

parts.examinerComment: The final volume depends on the amount of reactants, not the rate.

questions.stem: Fig. 3 shows the chromatogram of two dyes, A and B, and a mixture, X.

figures.alt: Chromatogram: the solvent front is 8.0 cm above the baseline. Dye A gives one spot at 2.0 cm, dye B one spot at 6.0 cm, and mixture X two spots at 2.0 cm and 6.0 cm.
figures.caption: Fig. 3

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the Rf value of dye B.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why the baseline must be drawn in pencil, not ink.

markingPoints.text: ink would dissolve in the solvent and separate, giving extra spots

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.
